intro: YAML to JSON turns YAML files (configuration for Docker Compose, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, OpenAPI or Ansible, for example) into JSON. Use it to pass a configuration to a tool that only understands JSON, to validate it against a JSON schema or to see clearly how a program interprets what you wrote in YAML.

Everything YAML 1.1 defines is honoured: block and inline lists and mappings, multi-line text with | and >, comments (which disappear, since JSON has none), anchors and aliases. Unquoted dates such as 2026-11-20 are written as ISO text, and keys that are not text (numbers or logical values) become text, as JSON requires.

If the file holds several documents separated by ---, the JSON is a list with one per document and we tell you so. Anchors and aliases are expanded, that is, each alias is replaced by a copy of its value.

We read YAML in safe mode: tags that in other programs create Python objects or run commands are rejected. We also count the values after expanding aliases and reject files that multiply beyond 2 million values (the well-known “billion laughs” bomb) or that contain themselves. Up to 25 MB per file and 20 per batch.

faq.a: Because in YAML 1.1 the unquoted words yes, no, on and off are logical values. If you want the text, write it in quotes: "no".
Yes, JSON does not support comments. If you need them, keep the original YAML too.
JSON to YAML turns JSON into readable YAML, with keys in their order.
